issues.description: Using @ts-ignore to suppress TypeScript errors defeats the purpose of type safety and hides potential issues with the import
issues.suggestion: Remove @ts-ignore and either: 1) Install proper type definitions (@types/neverchange), 2) Create a declaration file (neverchange.d.ts), or 3) Use a typed import with proper module declaration

issues.description: Global mutable state using 'let db: any' creates race conditions, is not thread-safe, and loses all type safety with 'any' type
issues.suggestion: Create a proper typed interface for the database and use a singleton pattern or dependency injection. Define: 'interface Database { execute(query: string, params?: any[]): Promise<void>; query(query: string, params?: any[]): Promise<any[]>; init(): Promise<void>; addMigrations(migrations: Migration[]): void; }' and type db as 'Database | null'

issues.description: Line 'if(db) db;' is a no-op that does nothing. This appears to be incomplete early-return logic that allows multiple database initializations
issues.suggestion: Replace with 'if (db) return;' or 'if (db) { return; }' to properly prevent re-initialization

issues.description: initDb() can be called multiple times concurrently, potentially causing race conditions or multiple initializations
issues.suggestion: Implement initialization guard with promise tracking: 'let initPromise: Promise<void> | null = null; export async function initDb() { if (initPromise) return initPromise; if (db) return; initPromise = _initDb(); return initPromise; }'

issues.description: Migration callbacks use 'any' type for db parameter, losing all type safety during critical database operations
issues.suggestion: Define a Migration interface: 'interface Migration { version: number; up: (db: Database) => Promise<void>; down?: (db: Database) => Promise<void>; }' and use it for the migrations array

issues.description: SQL queries throughout the file are vulnerable to SQL injection if the NeverChangeDB library doesn't properly handle parameterized queries. Additionally, there's no validation of input parameters
issues.suggestion: 1) Verify that NeverChangeDB properly sanitizes parameterized queries, 2) Add input validation for all parameters (check id is positive integer, text is non-empty string, etc.), 3) Consider using an ORM or query builder with built-in SQL injection protection

issues.description: addTodo() doesn't check if db is initialized before use, will throw runtime error if called before initDb()
issues.suggestion: Add initialization check at the start of each function: 'if (!db) throw new Error('Database not initialized. Call initDb() first.');' or create a helper function 'ensureDbInitialized()'

issues.description: Inconsistent error handling: addTodo catches and logs errors but doesn't throw, while updateTodo and deleteTodo catch, log, AND throw
issues.suggestion: Standardize error handling across all functions. Either: 1) Always throw errors to let callers handle them, or 2) Return Result types like { success: boolean; error?: string; data?: T }. Recommend throwing errors and letting callers handle UI concerns

issues.description: Using console.log/console.error for logging in library code is not production-ready and couples the code to console output
issues.suggestion: Use a proper logging library (winston, pino, etc.) or inject a logger interface: 'interface Logger { info(msg: string): void; error(msg: string, err?: Error): void; }' and pass it as a parameter or use a logging service

issues.description: getTodos() returns 'rows || []' but doesn't validate the structure of returned data. If db.query returns unexpected format, could cause runtime errors
issues.suggestion: Define a Todo interface: 'interface Todo { id: number; text: string; completed: boolean; deleted: boolean; }' and validate/parse the returned data: 'return (rows || []) as Todo[];' or use a runtime validation library like zod

issues.description: getTodos() returns all fields including 'deleted' which should be filtered out at the database level, exposing internal implementation details
issues.suggestion: Select only needed fields: 'SELECT id, text, completed FROM todos WHERE deleted = 0 ORDER BY id DESC' to follow principle of least privilege and reduce data transfer

issues.description: toggleTodo() doesn't return any indication of success or how many rows were affected. If id doesn't exist, function silently succeeds
issues.suggestion: Return the affected row count or the updated record: 'const result = await db.execute(...); if (result.changes === 0) throw new Error(`Todo with id ${id} not found`); return result;'

issues.description: toggleTodo() can toggle deleted todos since there's no WHERE deleted = 0 clause
issues.suggestion: Add deleted check: 'UPDATE todos SET completed = NOT completed WHERE id = ? AND deleted = 0'

issues.description: updateTodo() can update deleted todos and doesn't prevent empty text values
issues.suggestion: Add validation: 'if (!text?.trim()) throw new Error('Text cannot be empty'); await db.execute('UPDATE todos SET text = ? WHERE id = ? AND deleted = 0', [text.trim(), id]);'

issues.description: addTodo() doesn't validate that text parameter is non-empty, allowing empty todos to be created
issues.suggestion: Add input validation: 'if (!text || !text.trim()) throw new Error('Todo text cannot be empty'); const trimmedText = text.trim();' before inserting

issues.description: toggleTodo, updateTodo, and deleteTodo don't validate that id is a valid positive integer
issues.suggestion: Add validation helper: 'function validateId(id: number): void { if (!Number.isInteger(id) || id <= 0) throw new Error('Invalid id: must be positive integer'); }' and call at start of each function

issues.description: getTodos() fetches all non-deleted todos without pagination, which could cause performance issues with large datasets
issues.suggestion: Add pagination parameters: 'export async function getTodos(limit = 100, offset = 0) { return await db.query('SELECT * FROM todos WHERE deleted = 0 ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ? OFFSET ?', [limit, offset]); }'

issues.description: Database migrations are hardcoded in the initDb function, making it difficult to manage migrations as the application grows
issues.suggestion: Move migrations to a separate file (migrations.ts) and import them: 'import { migrations } from './migrations'; db.addMigrations(migrations);' This improves maintainability and testability

issues.description: No exported function to close/dispose of database connection, which could cause resource leaks
issues.suggestion: Add cleanup function: 'export async function closeDb(): Promise<void> { if (db?.close) { await db.close(); } db = null; }' and call it on application shutdown

issues.description: No JSDoc comments or documentation for exported functions, making API unclear for consumers
issues.suggestion: Add JSDoc comments for all exported functions documenting parameters, return types, thrown errors, and usage examples. Example: '/** * Adds a new todo item * @param text - The todo text (required, non-empty) * @returns Promise that resolves when todo is added * @throws Error if database is not initialized */'

issues.description: Inconsistent indentation in the addTodo function - the array parameter has unusual spacing
issues.suggestion: Use consistent formatting. Configure and use a code formatter like Prettier to maintain consistent code style

issues.description: Inconsistent spacing around array parameters - sometimes on new line, sometimes inline
issues.suggestion: Be consistent with formatting. Either always put array parameters inline for short queries or always on new line. Use Prettier for automatic formatting

issues.description: File lacks error boundaries and transaction support for operations that should be atomic
issues.suggestion: Add transaction support for multi-step operations: 'export async function withTransaction<T>(fn: (db: Database) => Promise<T>): Promise<T> { await db.execute('BEGIN TRANSACTION'); try { const result = await fn(db); await db.execute('COMMIT'); return result; } catch (err) { await db.execute('ROLLBACK'); throw err; } }'

codeQuality.summary: Critical type safety and security issues detected. The file has significant problems including: (1) Global mutable state with 'any' type losing all type safety, (2) Broken initialization check allowing re-initialization, (3) SQL injection vulnerability risk with missing input validation, (4) Functions don't check if database is initialized, (5) Inconsistent error handling patterns. The code needs immediate refactoring to add proper TypeScript types, input validation, consistent error handling, and proper database lifecycle management.

untestedPaths.reasoning: This line appears to be a bug. It should either return early if db exists or return the existing db instance. Currently it just evaluates db without doing anything, which means initDb() will reinitialize the database every time it's called.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that multiple initialization calls don't reinitialize the database

untestedPaths.reasoning: Core state mutation operation. Must verify it toggles completed status correctly in both directions and handles invalid IDs.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test toggling from incomplete to complete and vice versa, handling of invalid IDs

untestedPaths.reasoning: Core CRUD operation for updating todos. Must verify updates work correctly, handle special characters, validate parameters, and test error paths.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Core CRUD operation. Uses soft delete pattern. Must verify todo is marked as deleted (not removed), still exists in database, is filtered from getTodos(), and error handling works.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test soft-delete behavior, non-removal of record, exclusion from getTodos(), and error handling

untestedPaths.reasoning: If any function is called before initDb(), it will fail with cryptic errors. Need tests to verify graceful handling or clear error messages.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that all functions throw meaningful errors when database is not initialized

testCoverage.summary: ZERO test coverage. All 6 exported functions (initDb, addTodo, getTodos, toggleTodo, updateTodo, deleteTodo) are completely untested. This is a critical issue as they contain core database operations for a todo application. Major concerns: (1) Bug in initDb() line 7 that doesn't prevent reinitialization, (2) toggleTodo() lacks error handling, (3) No validation of SQL injection protection, (4) No tests for soft-delete behavior, (5) Missing tests for uninitialized database errors. Estimated 20+ test cases critically needed to ensure basic functionality and data integrity.

suggestions.description: Remove 'any' types and add proper TypeScript interfaces for type safety and better IDE support
suggestions.benefits: Type safety catches errors at compile time, improves IDE autocomplete, documents the data structures, and makes the code more maintainable

suggestions.description: Fix the broken initialization check that is a no-op
suggestions.benefits: Fixes a bug where the database could be re-initialized multiple times. The early return pattern is clearer and prevents unnecessary work

suggestions.description: Replace global mutable state with a singleton pattern or dependency injection for better testability
suggestions.before:
let db: any = null;
export async function addTodo(text: string) { await db.execute(...); }
suggestions.benefits: Encapsulation improves testability by allowing mock injection, provides explicit initialization checks, makes dependencies clear, and follows SOLID principles

suggestions.description: Extract the migrations array into a separate constant to separate configuration from logic
suggestions.after:
const MIGRATIONS = [{ version: 1, up: ... }, { version: 2, up: ... }];
db.addMigrations(MIGRATIONS);
suggestions.benefits: Separates configuration from logic, makes migrations easier to test and maintain, reduces function complexity

suggestions.description: Standardize error handling across inconsistent functions using a helper function
suggestions.before:
addTodo() { catch { console.error(...); } }
toggleTodo() { // no error handling }
suggestions.after: async executeWithErrorHandling<T>(operation, name) { try { return await operation(); } catch(e) { console.error(`${name} failed`, e); throw e; } }
suggestions.benefits: Consistent error handling makes debugging easier, removes code duplication, provides structured error information

suggestions.description: Remove console.log statements for successful operations or replace with proper logging
suggestions.after: // Remove or use proper logging framework
suggestions.benefits: Reduces noise in logs, follows separation of concerns, makes the code more reusable

suggestions.description: Extract SQL queries into constants to prevent typos and provide reusability
suggestions.before: const rows = await db.query('SELECT * FROM todos WHERE ...');
suggestions.after:
const SQL = { GET_TODOS: 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE ...', };
const rows = await db.query(SQL.GET_TODOS);
suggestions.benefits: Prevents SQL injection vulnerabilities from string concatenation, makes queries easier to maintain, provides autocomplete

suggestions.description: Add a getter function for the database instance with initialization check
suggestions.before: export async function addTodo(text: string) { await db.execute(...); }
suggestions.after:
function getDb(): Database { if (!db) throw new Error('DB not initialized'); return db; }
export async function addTodo(text: string) { await getDb().execute(...); }
suggestions.benefits: Provides explicit error messages when database is used before initialization, prevents null pointer errors

suggestions.description: Add input validation for all public functions to prevent invalid data
suggestions.before: export async function addTodo(text: string) { await db.execute('INSERT INTO todos (text) VALUES (?)', [text]); }
suggestions.after:
function validateTodoText(text: string): void { if (!text?.trim()) throw new Error('Text cannot be empty'); }
export async function addTodo(text: string) { validateTodoText(text); ... }
suggestions.benefits: Prevents invalid data from entering the database, provides clear error messages, improves data integrity

Medium-impact: Separate type-checking, add engines specification, update to stable ESLint version. recommendations.description: Fix critical bug on line 7 of src/db.ts where 'if(db) db;' is a no-op. Replace with 'if (db) return;' to prevent database re-initialization. Additionally, remove @ts-ignore and 'any' types, add proper TypeScript interfaces for Database, Todo, and Migration types.

Add comprehensive input validation to all database functions. Validate that todo text is non-empty, todo IDs are positive integers, and implement SQL injection protection. Update queries to include 'WHERE deleted = 0' checks in toggleTodo() and updateTodo().

ZERO test coverage detected. Create comprehensive test suite with critical priority: (1) initDb() initialization and re-initialization, (2) CRUD operations for all functions, (3) Error handling paths, (4) Uninitialized database error cases. Vitest is installed but no test files exist.

Add database initialization checks to all functions. Create a getDb() helper that throws descriptive errors if initDb() hasn't been called. Implement proper initialization guard with promise tracking to prevent race conditions during concurrent initDb() calls.

Standardize error handling across all CRUD functions. Currently inconsistent: addTodo() catches but doesn't throw, while updateTodo/deleteTodo catch, log, and throw. Create a reusable error handling helper function to maintain consistency.

Replace global mutable state with singleton pattern or class-based database service. This improves testability through dependency injection, provides explicit initialization checks, and makes dependencies clearer. Move hardcoded migrations to a separate migrations.ts file.

Remove console.log statements for successful operations and use proper logging infrastructure. Configure Prettier for consistent code formatting. Add JSDoc documentation for all exported functions explaining parameters, return types, and error conditions.

Update eslint-plugin-react-hooks from RC version (^5.1.0-rc.0) to stable (^5.1.0). Review neverchange dependency at version 0.0.1 for stability. Implement 'npm audit' in CI/CD pipeline and regular dependency auditing.
Add 'engines' field to package.json (Node >=18.0.0, npm >=9.0.0). Add separate type-check script. Add clean script for build reproducibility. Add repository, author, and license metadata fields.

Add return type annotations (Promise<Todo[]>) and runtime validation for data structures. Implement transaction support for atomic operations. Add database cleanup function (closeDb()) to prevent resource leaks. Add pagination to getTodos() to handle large datasets.
